transcript:
Dr: Patient Maria Rodriguez, 45-year-old female here for diabetes follow-up. A1C today is 7.2, down from 7.8 three months ago.
Dr: She reports good medication adherence. Taking metformin 500mg twice daily. No hypoglycemic episodes.
Dr: Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 72, BMI 29.1. Foot exam normal, monofilament testing intact.
Dr: Assessment: Type 2 diabetes, improving control. Plan: Continue metformin 500mg BID. Recheck A1C in 3 months. Reinforce diet and exercise.

transcript:
Dr: Mrs. Carter, before we update your chart for today, do you have any drug allergies or food allergies on file?
Patient: No, none at all. I've never had a reaction to any medication, never been told I had a food allergy. Nothing.
Dr: Got it. I'll record that as NKDA, no known drug allergies. Good to have on the record.
Patient: Sure.
Dr: Now for today, what's bringing you in?
Patient: Just my routine hypertension follow-up. My home cuff's been showing 130 over 84, 132 over 86, in that range.
Dr: Okay. Let me check today. Vitals show BP 132 over 84, HR 70, BMI 26.4. You're tolerating the lisinopril 10mg once daily?
Patient: Yes, every morning. No cough, no dizziness.
Dr: Assessment: stable essential hypertension on lisinopril monotherapy. Plan: continue lisinopril 10mg po daily, recheck in three months, keep logging at home.
Patient: Sounds good.
